alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 9:56PM MDT until October 23 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall across the area is
occurring.

* WHERE...South Central La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 948 PM MDT, Gauge reports the La Plata River has risen above
flood stage due to heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly in the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of
rain have fallen across the area over the past two days.
- This includes the La Plata River and the surrounding low areas
near the river.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hesperus.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 9:50PM MDT until October 24 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and Utah,
including the following areas, Arches/Grand Flat,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...Through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recent burn scars and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Flooding is imminent or ongoing with additional rounds of showers
and thunderstorms expected through Friday afternoon. Rivers and
creeks may still experience high waters even after rainfall has
ended.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 9:44PM MDT until October 23 at 2:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Western Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern Hinsdale County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 200 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 939 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in
the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
La Plata River, Animas River, Vallecito Creek, Taylor Creek, Los
Pinos River, Florida River, and First Fork Piedra River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Durango, La Plata, Falfa, Hesperus, Bondad, Breen, Mayday, Kline,
Marvel, Redmesa and Vallecito.
- Flooding along the Animas River, including areas on the north
side of Durango, is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Rivers
and streams will continue to rise through the night, with peak
flow expected Friday afternoon.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 5:22PM MDT until October 23 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
occurring.

* WHERE...Southeastern La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until midnight MDT Tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding with road washouts also occurring.
Streams and dry washes continue to rise due to excess runoff from
earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 520 PM MDT, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring. Between 1.5 and 2
inches of rain have fallen over the last 24 hours.
- This includes but is not limited to the following streams
anddrainages...
Florida River, Spring Creek, Ute Creek, Salt Creek and Dry Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Bayfield, Ignacio, Oxford, Tiffany and Allison.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

planned_events.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147600
planned_events.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting October 24, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until October 24, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 24, 7:00AM - October 24, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
